en: In the mountain cave of Rṇa, I worship the Śrī-pādukā of the goddess Bhagamālinī, who is the essence of Oḍiśanātha and the power of Brahmā.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃ Kilhrh Skhlhr Sklhrīṃ. In the Brahma-cakra at the Oḍiyāna-pīṭha, I worship the sandals of the goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, who is the essence of Caryānātha and the supreme power whose self is Brahman. Bali.
Hsoṃ Hsklhrīṃ Hsauṃ, I worship the sandals of Mahātripurabhairavī. [Offer] the bali.

Nirvāṇacchāya || KṢAṂ KṢAṂ KṢAṂ HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the sandals for Trailokyameruaṅkuśāyī. AiṂ (5) KṢĀṂ, the sandals for Nirvāṇeśvarānandanātha; KṢMLVRYĪṂ HRĪṂ ŚRĪṂ, for the benefit of Paramanirvāṇe [Śakti].
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to the deity Nirvāṇanātha Śkṣmlvryū-īṃ, to the one accompanied by the power (śakti) of the Sovereign of Supreme Nirvāṇa (Paramanirvāṇeśvarī), [I offer] the sandals (pādukā).

Hakṣa-hakṣa-hakṣa HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. To the Great Mantra of seventy million syllables, to the Hook of the Meru of the Three Worlds, homage to the sandals! Aiṃ (5). We know her who is stainless; we meditate on her who is formless; may she, the Void, inspire us! Aiṃ (5). HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ. Homage to the sandals of all authority! [Offer] the great bali-offering to Tvaḥ!
Aiṃ (5) Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ! O Kṣetrapāla, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṁ (5) Śrīṁ Hrīṁ! O Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṃ (5) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Ga! O Kulagaṇeśvara, accept this offering (bali)! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ! O Mahākālavīra, Lord of the Great Cremation Ground, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṁ (5) Hskhphrūṁ, O Śrī Siddhicāmuṇḍā, accept this bali offering; svāhā! (2)
Aiṁ (5) To the Ākāśacāraṇīs and the group of letters beginning with Śa, accept this offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṃ (5). To all beings, to all piśācas, and to all beloved deities, accept this worship and this offering—svāhā! (2).

Aiṃ, the mantra-deity; Hrīṃ, the mantra-deity; Śrīṃ, the mantra-deity; Khphreṃ, the mantra-deity; Hsauṃ, the mantra-deity. Ka kha ga gha ṅa, ca cha ja jha ña, ṭa ṭha ḍa ḍha ṇa, ta tha da dha na, pa pha ba bha ma, ya ra la va, śa ṣa sa ha kṣa.

a ā i ī u ū ṛ ṝ ḷ ḹ e ai o au aṃ aḥ || From us, in the venerable Caturāmnāya, [salutation] to Naṇḍanātha Bhaṭṭārikā, to the Western Jyeṣṭhā, to the Great Māyā Śrī Kubjikā Devī, and to the goddess Śrī Siddhilakṣmī, in the venerable Caturāmnāya.
O Śrīmitriśānandanātha, for the sake of the daily worship, the offering of bali, and the ritual adoration of the forms of the Bhartṛkāris, accept this worship and this bali—svāhā! (2)
Perform the invocation and other rites, display the *yonimudrā*, and offer incense, lamps, food offerings (*naivedya*), recite the mantra (*japa*), and chant the hymn of praise (*stotra*).

The sixteen commands of Śrī Saṃvartā; the slayer [Hantā] in the Akha-kha [mantra]; the red garment; the Piśācī; Mahāmāyā; the syllable *U*; Brahmāṇī standing in the center; the lion-faced one; the syllable *Kvā*; the syllable *Aiṃ*; and likewise, according to the tradition, the extraction of the *pahārā* [mantras], and so forth. The offering (*tarpaṇa*) for the shadow of the pledge (*samaya*), whether single or manifold.
For the purpose of dismissing the bali offering.
[Thus ends the procedure for the daily ritual of worshiping the deities and the bali offering according to the ancient tradition. Auspicious!
Then, Tumbheśvarī.
The Guru’s blessing. The ritual placement (*nyāsa*): Aiṃ (5) HSKṢMLVRYAṂ ASTRĀYA PHAṬ—purification of the hands.

Hskṣmlvryaṃ aṅguṣṭhāya namaḥ | Hskṣmlvryīṃ tarjanyāyai svāhā | Hskṣmlvryaṃ madhyamāyai vauṣaṭ | Aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryaṃ anāmikāyai hūṃ | Aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryaṃ kaniṣṭhikāyai vaṣaṭ | Aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryaṃ astrāyai phaṭ | This is the Kara-nyāsa. Thva (*).

Aṅganyāsa: [Perform the assignment of limbs]. For the seat of the water vessel: *pādukāṃ*. *Hskṣmlvryaṃ hskṣmlvryaṃ*, *śrījalapātrabhaṭṭārikāyai pādukāṃ*. Having worshipped with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*), perform the invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth, and the *dhenumudrā*.
Aiṃ (5). We know Ugracaṇḍā; we meditate upon Durgā; may Caṇḍī inspire us.
Śrī Śaṃvarta: Invocation. The Three Deities. Brahmāṇī and the others. Pādukā for Haṃsāsana.
Aiṃ (5) A, [I worship] the sandals of Brahmāṇī and Aśitāṅgabhairava, and so forth... the sandals for the one seated upon a buffalo; the sandals for the one seated upon a lion. Then, the meditation.
The goddess has eighteen arms; she possesses full breasts, chest, and thighs. She holds a skull-bowl, a sword, a bell, a shield, a raised index finger (tarjanī), and a bow.
In his left hands, he shines with a banner, a hand-drum, and a noose;
likewise, [he holds] a sword, a spear, a corpse, a goad, and a terrifying vajra.
Holding a mace in her right hand that illuminates the world,
she is adorned with various ornaments and possesses a splendor equal to ten million suns.
Mounted upon a lion, he is majestic, the bestower of the fruits of all desires;
adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, a crown, and a diadem, he blazes with splendor.
Adorned with all ornaments and saluted by all the gods—
having meditated thus upon the Great Goddess, who bestows the fruit of one's desired aims.
Thus, salutation to the flower of meditative concentration.
The sandals for the elephant-throne; the sandals for the lion-throne.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hskṣmlvryaṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, [I offer] the sandals to the Goddess Jayatumbeśvarī.
Three *añjali* gestures (3). The six-limbed offering (*ṣaḍaṅga-bali*).

To the one of great power who shakes [all things], [perform] the invocation and so forth, and the *yonimudrā*. "Obeisance to the venerable Lord," and so forth. Incense. Lamp. Recitation (*jāpa*). *Tide*. *Hskhphrūṃ Śkhphrūṃ* (ten times).
Hskṣmlvryaṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ (10). Japa for Malinaya: Hsklīṃ Śklīṃ (54). *Nirvāṇa* (54) Stotra.
Śrī Śaṃvartā; the letter *U*; Brahmāṇī; three in the middle; or there may be six, reddish-yellow in color.
"Resembling the glow of the bandhūka flower," and so forth. Herein are the perfumes and other offerings. The *pretas* are both singular and plural.
Thus ends the worship of the deity Paścimatuṃbeśvarī.
Then, Mahākāla.
Salutation to the Gurus. Nyāsa: Aiṃ (5) Hraṃḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
The wealth of the hands: *hrāṃ* salutation to the thumb; *hrīṃ* *svāhā* to the index finger.
Hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the middle finger; Hreṃ, hūṃ to the ring finger; Hrāṃ, vaṣaṭ to the little finger.

Hraṁḥ astrāya phaṭ || Aiṁ (5) hrāṁ hṛdayāya namaḥ || Aiṁ (5) hrīṁ śirase svāhā || Aiṁ (5) hrūṁ śikhāyai vauṣaṭ || Aiṁ (5) hreṁ kavacāya hūṁ || Aiṁ (5) hroṁ netratrayāya vaṣaṭ || Aiṁ (5) hraḥ astrāya phaṭ || Pādukā for the seat of the water-vessel. Root mantra. Six-limbed ritual (ṣaḍaṅga).
The invocation and other rites are performed with the Dhenu-mudrā. The Gāyatrī mantra is: *śikhānāthāya vidmahe śvanadāya dhīmahe tanno rudraḥ pracodayāt*.
Salutation to the seat of the argha vessel. [Recite] the root mantra. Having performed worship with the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅga).
Invocation and so forth; the Yoni-mudrā; purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi); self-worship; invocation of Śrī Saṃvartānā;
the three deities; the sandals for the seat of the preta; meditation.
Aiṃ (5). Seated upon a great corpse-throne, red and black with great brilliance, having one face and three eyes, terrifying, with tawny hair standing erect on his head.
O you with tawny eyes, tawny eyebrows, and tawny hair; O you of massive body and great feverous radiance!
You who are clothed in a tiger skin and wear a lion skin as an upper garment.
Adorned with a necklace of human bones, black anklets, and other ornaments,
he holds a sword and a skull-bowl in his hands, and carries a vessel marked with drops and a khaṭvāṅga staff.
Possessing a great splendor like ten million flashes of lightning, adorned with a garland of speed,
her sandals are rubbed by the heads of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and the lords of the gods.
It was filled with the cries of jackals, ravens, owls,
and vultures, and resounded with the tumultuous "kil-kil" shrieks of *bhūtas*, *pretas*, and *piśācas*.
And in the cremation ground, she is most fierce, adorned by a host of yoginīs;
O Mahādeva, you who always delight in the welfare of the worlds.
I meditate upon the illustrious Mahākāla, the Bhairava and Lord of the World;
whether one hears this on the path or causes others to hear it with a concentrated mind, [one attains the goal].
One attains all perfections and the constant increase of victory.
Thus ends the flower of meditative concentration. Name.
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ! To Mahākāla, the Great Terrifier, the crusher of all beings, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Pādukā for the one who has come forth. Aiṃ (5) Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ, pādukā for the venerable Śikhā-Svacchanda-Mahābhairava. [Six-limbed ritual] Offering.
Aiṃ (5) Pādukāṃ to Hetuka Bhairava. Aiṃ (5) Pādukāṃ to Tripurāntaka Bhairava.
(5) Pādukā to Agnivetālabhairava. Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to Agnijihvābhairava.
Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to Kālākṣabhairava. Aiṃ (5) Pādukā to Kalālinabhairava.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Ekapādabhairava; Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Bhīmarūpabhairava.
Aiṁ (5) to Hātakabhairava, the sandals! Aiṁ (5) to Acalabhairava, the sandals!
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Aśitāṅgabhairava; Aṃ (5) the sandals for Rurubhairava.
Aṃ (5) to Caṇḍabhairava, the sandals! Aṃ (5) to Kroḍhabhairava, the sandals!
Aṃ (5) the sandals for Unmattabhairava; Aṃ (5) the sandals for Kapālīsabhairava.
Aṃ (5) the sandals of Bhīṣaṇabhairava; Aṃ (5) the sandals of Saṃhārabhairava.
The *bali* for all these [deities]. Three handfuls (*añjali*) with the root mantra (*mūlamantra*). The six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*). The *bali*. Shaking the great *bali* of Tvaṣṭṛ.
The invocation (*āvāhana*) and so forth. The *yonimudrā*. Homage to Śrīnātha; homage to Śrīsiddhinātha;
homage to Śrīkujyasanātha; repeated salutations!
Then follows the worship of the goddess Ugracaṇḍā.
Salutation to the Guru for the sake of illumination:
*śkṣmlvryīṃ*, the sandals of the Noble Lady (*Bhaṭṭārikā*) of the sequence of ritual placement (*nyāsa*). On the crown:
*tānamoṣasa*. *Aiṃ*, the sandals of the Lotus Seat (*Padmāsana*). Meditation.
Aiṁ (5). Seated upon a lotus throne, with ten faces including the face of a corpse, possessing three eyes, six-colored, of great brilliance, and endowed with all the auspicious marks.
The eastern face is the color of gold, while the southern is adorned with black;
the northern should be yellow in color, and the one above that is resplendent with red.
To the south of the red [line] is the smoke-colored [line], and to the north is the white one.
Above that is yellow in color; to the right of the yellow is black, and to the north is red—so they say; above that is white, which is most excellent.
The god has eighteen arms and is adorned with a garland of headless trunks.
The god holds a sword, a pheketā weapon, a trident, and likewise a goad;
he also holds a thread, a water-pot, a bell, a hand-drum, and a skull-topped staff.
A bow well-joined with a string, adorned with a bamboo shaft and a bell.
He holds a discus and a mace in his hands, while his other two hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
The deity, bearing the bindu upon the letter *ka* and adorned with various ornaments,
is well-seated in a blissful posture upon a corpse-seat as his throne.

Thus, a person who applies themselves with a disciplined mind should meditate upon this ninefold mandala of the self, which is the mandala of the Guru; such a human being shall attain swift accomplishment.
Thus ends the homage to the flower of meditative concentration.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. To the venerable Navātma Śrīgurumaṇḍalabhaṭṭārikā, the empowerment of bliss, the joy of Bhairava, and the sovereign of heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ: [I offer] the sandals.
In the center of the mandala, one should bow down to oneself.
Aiṃ (5) Nlūṃ E. This great worship [is offered] to the sandals of Śrī Kubjikā, the Guru-maṇḍala.
Aiṃ (5) Mlūṃ I. This is the great worship; the sandals of the venerable Śakti of the Guru-maṇḍala.
Aiṁ (5) Plūṁ Ū: the sandals of the Śrī Devī of the Parameṣṭhī-guru-maṇḍala.
Aiṃ (5) Slūṃ I, the sandals of the assembly of supreme gurus, the venerable Jñānāyī.
Aiṃ (5) Glūṃ A Gurumaṇḍala Śrī-Ājñāyai Pādukāṃ.
Aiṃ (5) [I worship] the sandals of the Supreme Goddess, who is the maṇḍala of the Guru of the essence of Śiva.
Aiṃ (5). The sandals of the Śrīvidyā-tattva Guru-maṇḍala for the Goddess Parāparā.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī-Ātmatattva-gurumaṇḍala, the sandals for Aparā.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals to Ājñākusumā.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals of Śrī Jayā.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals of Śrī Vijayā. Aiṁ (5) the sandals of Śrī Ajitā.
Aiṃ (5) to the venerable Aparājitā, the sandals! Aiṃ (5) śrī haṃ to the venerable Śāntāntitā, the sandals!
Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ Yaṃ, the sandals of Śāntā. Aiṃ (5) Śrī Laṃ, the sandals of Vidyā.
Aiṁ (5) Śrī Vaṁ, the sandals for Pratiṣṭhā; Aiṁ (5) Śrī Raṁ, the sandals for Nivṛtti.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals of Śrī Kulabhairavā. Aiṃ (5) the sandals of Śrī Kulanāthabhairavā.

The sandals of Śrī Kulatumburubhairavā. Aiṃ (5) The sandals of Śrī Kulakapāṭakabhairavā. Aiṃ (5) The sandals of Śrī Kula-ājñābhairavā. Aiṃ (5) The sandals of Śrī Kula-ājñādevī. Aiṃ (5) Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ, the sandals of Kṣatrapālā.
Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, the sandals of Kulaputra Vaṭukanātha.
Aiṃ (5) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ, the sandals of Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara.
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Śrīṃ Mahākomārikā Vicce Pādukāṃ. [Offer three handfuls of water with the root mantra. 3.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ. To the venerable Navātma-gurumaṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā, who is empowered by the hero Ānandaśakti-bhairava-ānanda, [I offer] the sandals: Śkṣmlvryīṃ. Pādukāṃ.
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ, the sandals of the venerable Navātma-gurumaṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā.

Aiṁ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṁ Śkṣmlvryīṁ. To the venerable Navātma-guru-maṇḍala-bhaṭṭārikā, [who is] the empowerment of the hero for the bliss of Ānanda-śakti-bhairava-ānanda, Hskṣmlvryūṁ Śkṣmlvryīṁ— [I offer] the sandals.
Having performed the worship with the six limbs (6), [offer] the bali with that same [mantra].
Aiṁ (5) Aghore Hrāṁ, Thaghohrīṁ, Ghorantare Hūṁ Phreṁ, Sarvvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṁ Ju Saḥ Hroṁ, O you who possess the form of Rudra, Hraḥ! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyākarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ So Saḥ Pādukāṃ.

Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṃ chīṃ! Kiṇi (2)! Vicce! [I offer] the sandals. With this, the *bali* offering.

Aiṃ (5). The sandals of the entire seat of mantras, the lion-throne seat, the seats and secondary seats, the fields and secondary fields, the gathering places and secondary gathering places, the divine accomplishments, and the wheel of the samaya.
Aiṁ (5). Whatever has been said or not said, all that—Aiṁ—to the Heart, the sandals.
After the invocation and other rites, one should display the *yonimudrā*. [Recite] "Obeisance to Śrīnātha," and so forth.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the worship of Navātman.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Padmāsanā. Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ the sandals for the lineage of Śrī Gurus and for Bhaktāri. Bali.

Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Padmāsanā. Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYŪ-ĪṂ ŚRĪ- the sandals for the venerable Oṣadhīkramabhaṭṭārikā. The offering (bali). Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Vṛṣāsanā. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Siṃhāsanā. Aiṃ.
(5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda, for the empowerment of the Hero, ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ; the sandals of Śrīkaṇṭhanātha together with his own Śakti. Bali.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Haṃsāsana; Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Vṛṣāsana.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals for her who has the peacock-throne; Aiṁ (5) the sandals for her who has the garuḍa-throne.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for her who has the buffalo as her seat. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for her who has the elephant as her seat.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the one seated upon the corpse-throne. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the one seated upon the human-throne.
Aiṁ (5). To Aghorā, the unfailing, the bestower of boons, the stainless Śrī Brahmāṇī, Vicce, [I offer] the sandals and the sacrificial offering.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Śrīmāheśvari, Vicce, [I worship] the sandal.
Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Śrīkomārī, Vicce—[the sandals].
Aiṃ (5) Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Śrīvaiṣṇavi, Vicce, [worship] the sandals!
Aiṃ (5) Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Śrīvārāhī, Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) O Aghorā, O Unfailing One, O Giver of Boons, O Stainless One, O Śrī-Indrāṇī, O Vicce! [I worship] the sandal.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Śrīcāmuṇḍā, Vicce, [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vimale, Śrīmāhālakṣmī, Vicce, [worship] the sandals and the offering.
All these [are] Brahmāṇī and the others, eight [in number].
Aiṃ (5) the sandals of Aghora-śakti. Aiṃ (5) the sandals of Anantāsana.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals for Kaṇḍā Sanāyā. Aiṁ (5) the sandals for Nārāsanāyā.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the seat of petals. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the seat of filaments.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals to her seated upon the pericarp. Aiṁ (5) the sandals to her seated upon the lotus.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for her who is seated upon the buffalo throne. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for her who is seated upon the lion throne.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the seat of Śumbha. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the seat of Niśumbha.
Aiṁ (5) Namaḥ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Caṇḍacogrāyai Namaḥ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Pādukāṁ || Bāliṁ ||
The sandal of the goddess Śrī Rudracaṇḍā; the sandal of the goddess Śrī Pracaṇḍā.
The sandal of the venerable goddess Caṇḍogrā; the sandal of the venerable goddess Caṇḍakā.
The sandal of the venerable goddess Caṇḍā; the venerable goddess Caṇḍavatī;
the sandal of the venerable goddess Caṇḍarūpā.
The sandals of the goddess Śrī-Aticaṇḍikā. Aiṃ (5). The sandals for the one seated upon the buffalo.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the lion-throne. Aiṃ (5) Oṃ hrīṃ rājaprade hsphreṃ ugracaṇḍe ripumardanī hūṃ phreṃ, always protect (2) you and me; juṃ saḥ, O remover of death, the sandals!
I worship the offering. I worship the bali.

Aiṃ (5) the sandals for Padmāsanā. Aiṃ (5) Liṅgaṇḍi Piṅgaṇḍī Kuru (2) Kaṇḍāyai Svāhā; Vāgīśvarī, Vṛddhi, Mahantārikā, Vicce—the sandals. The offering (bali). One should perform the invocation and other rites and display the Yonimudrā.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals of Ādhāraśakti. Aiṁ (5) the sandals of Anantāsana. The sandals of Kaṇḍāsana. Aiṁ (5) the sandals of Nārāsana.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals for the lotus-seat. Aiṁ (5) the sandals for the filament-seat.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for her seated upon the pericarp. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for her seated upon the lotus.
Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the seat of the five pretas. Aiṃ (5) the sandals for the corpse-seat.
Aiṁ (5) the sandals for the one seated upon the bull-throne. Aiṁ (5) the sandals for the one seated upon the lion-throne.
Aiṃ (5) Hsauṃ Svāhā! [I offer] the sandals to the one seated upon the fire-pretas.

Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorante Hūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hreṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hroṃ Rudra, the sandals! Vajra Kubjinī Hsphreṃ, the attractor of the three worlds, Hrīṃ, the witherer of the limbs of desire!
Vanī [the devourer], the one who performs the act of eating: Aiṃ Soḥ Saḥ, [I offer] the venerable pādukā and the bali.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One! Hsphreṃ (**). To the Body: Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Not-Terrible One, O You Whose Face is Not-Terrible!
Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi (2)! Vicce! [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ! Ṅa Ña Ṇa! O you of fierce countenance! Chāṃ Chīṃ Kiṇi (2)! Vicce! [I worship] the sandals.
Aiṃ (5) Bhagavati Siddhe Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ Kubjike Śrāṃ Śrīṃ Śrūṃ Khage Aiṃ Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhi Kiṇi (2) Vicce Pādukāṃ.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśaktibhā, the empowerment of bliss; Śkṣmlvryīṃ!
To the venerable Aṣṭāviṃśatikrama-bhaṭṭārikā, the sandals!
